def ir(self, state, xmin=900, xmax=1700, normal_modes: bool = False):

    """ Plots the IR spectrum in xmin -- xmax range,
    x-axis is multiplied by scaling factor, everything
    is normalized to 1. If exp_data is specified,
    then the top panel is getting plotted too.
    Need to add output directory. Default name is self._id
    """

    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    from matplotlib.ticker import NullFormatter
    import math

    colors = self.colors
    background_colors = []

    for color in colors:
        color[0] += 0.25
        color[1] += 0.25
        color[2] += 0.25
        background_colors.append(color)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, figsize=(math.ceil(10 * (xmax - xmin) / (1500)), 3))

    self.gaussian_broadening(state, resolution=0.001, broaden=2)

    # left, width = 0.02, 0.98 ; bottom, height = 0.15, 0.8
    # ax  = [left, bottom, width, height ]
    # ax  = plt.axes(ax)
    exten = 20

    ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='both', bottom=True, top=False, labelbottom=True, right=False, left=False,
                   labelleft=False)
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False);
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False);
    ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
    ax.xaxis.set_tick_params(direction='out')
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(NullFormatter())
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.1)

    xticks = np.linspace(xmin, xmax, int((xmax - xmin + 2 * exten) / 100) + 1)
    ax.set_xticks(xticks)
    ax.set_xticklabels([int(x) for x in xticks], fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlim(xmin - exten, xmax + exten + 10)

    shift = 0.05
    incr = (state.IR[-1, 0] - state.IR[0, 0]) / (len(state.IR) - 1)
    scale_t = 1 / np.amax(state.IR[int(xmin / incr):int(xmax / incr) + 100, 1])

    Xsc = state.IR[:, 0];
    IRsc = state.IR[:, 1] * scale_t
    ir_theo = ax.plot(Xsc, IRsc + shift, color='k', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.fill_between(Xsc, np.linspace(shift, shift, len(IRsc)), IRsc + shift, color=background_colors[0], alpha=0.5)

    if normal_modes == True:
        for l in range(len(state.Freq)):
            ax.plot([state.Freq[l], state.Freq[l]], [shift, state.Ints[l] * scale_t + shift], linewidth=2,
                    color=colors[0])

    fig.tight_layout()
    current_path = os.getcwd()

The mlmd interface provides geometry minimization, equilibration, production dynamics, checkpoint restart, periodic solvation, and one-dimensional metadynamics analysis. Its configuration classes are nested under mlmd; simulation dependencies load only when required.

State.element_symbol, StateBuilder.element_symbol, and InputBuilder.element_number wrap these mappings; they do not supply atomic masses. See element utilities.

docs.title: Units, indexing, and scientific conventions
docs.text: Use these conventions when transferring data between matmalib, simulation engines, notebooks, and other analysis packages. Numeric arrays carry values; attributes such as time_unit describe those values and do not generally convert them.

docs.title: Coordinates, indices, and shared objects
docs.text:
Concept Convention Molecular coordinates Finite (n_atoms, 3) array, one row per atom. Ring coordinates Finite (..., 5, 3) or (..., 6, 3) array in cyclic order. Trajectory coordinates Full-system frames with a fixed atom count and order. Glycan/conformer ring, membership, and selection indices Zero-based positions in state.atoms, independent of Atom.id. Monomer indices Zero-based positions in glycan.monomers; used in link donor/acceptor fields, trajectory column names, and SNFG positions. Cluster member/representative indices Positions in the original input ensemble, including when some states are excluded. Glycan construction from a state Retains metadata and shares existing Atom objects. Representative Space New container sharing the chosen State objects.

Legacy StateEditor distance/angle edits, determine_carried_atoms, and State.connectivity_matrix require each atom.id to equal its position in state.atoms. Dihedral measurements and edits use atom-list positions independently of Atom.id. See geometry prerequisites before editing a manually constructed or renumbered state.

Ring order is not just a set of vertices. Automatic sugar rings begin at O, continue to the anomeric carbon, then follow the remaining ring carbons. Aldoses begin at C1 after O; ketoses begin at C2. Monomers are sorted by their smallest ring atom index. Explicit rings must preserve a consistent starting point and traversal direction for meaningful comparisons.

Explicit monomer assignments do not automatically generate chemical atom names or link metadata. See Glycans for the distinction between geometric assignment and chemical detection.

State-based checks compare element sequences, but they cannot detect swapping two atoms of the same element. Arrays carry no element metadata. These interfaces do not perform symmetry matching, atom mapping, or topology repair.

docs.title: Length, angle, time, and energy units
docs.text:
Quantity Convention XYZ coordinates No unit conversion on reading; supplied geometries normally use angstroms. Sugar bond detection distXX=1.65, distXH=1.15, assuming angstroms. Change cutoffs or supply trusted connectivity for other units. CP Q, q2, q3 Same length unit as input coordinates. CP planarity threshold planar_tolerance=1e-6 in coordinate length units. CP angles Degrees by default; degrees=False selects radians. Ring-classification distance and carppy_theta Always degrees, including with degrees=False. StateEditor / State internal angles and dihedrals Always degrees; dihedrals use the signed atan2 convention below. Glycosidic/backbone torsions Degrees by default; degrees=False selects radians; result records angle_unit. RMSD and cluster threshold Input coordinate length units. Trajectory timestep Interval between saved frames; default unit label fs. Standalone times / time_unit Explicit values and descriptive unit; no rescaling just because the label changes. CP2K XYZ CP reader Requires timestep; uses fs and ignores comment-line times. Time-series plot display fs → ps, ps → ns, ns unchanged. The underlying Data values remain unchanged. Cluster energy_unit Units of stored scalar state energies: hartree (default), kcal/mol, or kJ/mol. Cluster energy_window Always kcal/mol above the minimum. CP sphere temp Kelvin, default 300. CP sphere energy_unit kcal/mol (default) or kJ/mol for the population-derived energy grid.

For mixed sources, normalize coordinates and energy values before combining them. A unit label does not make values compatible. The Data.from_file CP2K adapter does not expose arbitrary time units; use cremer_pople_trajectory for explicit nonuniform times and another unit label.

docs.title: Cremer–Pople coordinates
docs.text:
For an ordered ring with positions indexed by j=0,...,N-1, coordinates are centered at the ring centroid. The mean-plane normal is the normalized cross product R_sine × R_cosine. Heights z_j are projections onto that normal. The second-mode components follow

q2 * cos(phi) =  sqrt(2/N) * sum_j(z[j] * cos(4*pi*j/N))
q2 * sin(phi) = -sqrt(2/N) * sum_j(z[j] * sin(4*pi*j/N))

For six-membered rings,

q3 = sum_j((-1)**j * z[j]) / sqrt(6)
Q = sqrt(q2**2 + q3**2)
theta = atan2(q2, q3)

Five-membered rings have Q=q2 and no q3 or theta. Phi is normalized to [0, 360) or [0, 2π); theta to [0, 180] or [0, π]. Starting-atom changes, traversal reversals, and reflections alter angular conventions. Proper rigid rotations and translations do not.

Undefined angles are represented by NaN: phi for a planar ring or pure chair, theta for a planar ring. Zero amplitude is different from an undefined mean plane: collapsed or collinear coordinates can make the plane degenerate and raise ValueError.

docs.title: Canonical pucker names are positional
docs.text:
Six-membered classification uses 38 CarPpy reference vectors of three transformed diagonal dihedrals. Its carppy_theta is a three-component vector, not the scalar CP polar theta. Its reference distance is Euclidean distance in that three-angle space, in degrees.

For the standard oxygen-first six-membered order, labels use 1–5 for the carbon positions after O and 6 for O. For an aldopyranose these coincide with C1–C5. For a ketose, they describe ring positions rather than chemical carbon numbering. The sphere plot writes O instead of 6 in its ideal-position annotations.

Five-membered labels use positions 0–4 in supplied ring order and nearest envelope/twist phase. Their distance is the shortest wrapped phase difference in degrees. Do not compare the five- and six-membered distances as if they were the same metric.

planar indicates amplitude below the configured tolerance. unassigned means the closest reference exceeded max_distance; nearest_label and the nearest family remain available. These are shape classifications, not energy estimates, proof of stability, or population measurements.

See Puckering for synthetic examples that reproduce known coordinates and demonstrate rejection tolerances.

docs.title: Torsion definitions
docs.text:
StateEditor.get_dihedral, four-atom measure/measure_internal calls, and glycan torsions use the same signed convention. For coordinates a, b, c, d, let u be the unit vector from b toward c, and project the two terminal vectors onto the plane perpendicular to u:

u = (c - b) / norm(c - b)
v = (a - b) - dot(a - b, u) * u
w = (d - c) - dot(d - c, u) * u
dihedral = atan2(dot(cross(u, v), w), dot(v, w))

Convert the result to degrees for StateEditor; its range is [-180, 180]. Positive angles follow a right-handed rotation from v toward w about u. For a=(0,1,0), b=(0,0,0), c=(1,0,0), and d=(1,0,1), the result is +90°. Reflecting all z coordinates changes it to −90°; a rigid translation or proper rotation preserves it. Reversing the entire four-atom order also preserves the angle. Exact 0° and ±180° are valid; coincident central atoms or collinear triples make a torsion undefined and raise ValueError.

The legacy StateEditor sign has been corrected to this convention, including a translation-dependent sign bug. Glycan and ring-analysis conventions are unchanged. For saved legacy measurements, recompute from coordinates rather than assuming every value needs only a sign flip. The interactive geometry tutorial demonstrates the corrected sign and translation invariance.

Glycosidic phi is donor ring O–anomeric C–linking O–acceptor C. Psi continues through the preceding acceptor backbone carbon, using its ring O for an anomeric acceptor. Terminal-carbon glycosidic omega is linking O–terminal C–ring C–ring O. Hydroxymethyl backbone omega lists those four atoms in the reverse order.

Always compare the reported atom_indices quadruplets as well as angle names. “Phi,” “psi,” and “omega” do not by themselves establish a universal definition across programs. Backbone omega is None for missing or ambiguous terminal oxygens; a glycosidic omega key is absent when that linkage has no corresponding terminal-carbon torsion.

docs.title: Periodic boundaries and trajectories
docs.text:
Puckering, RMSD, and glycan torsion routines do not apply periodic-boundary corrections. Supply whole, unwrapped molecules or rings. Atoms split across a cell boundary may look far apart, break bond detection, or generate meaningless geometrical values even if all entries are finite.

Trajectory assignments are fixed at the reference/first frame. They are appropriate for a consistent atom ordering and topology, not a reactive trajectory that changes connectivity. Coordinate generators are consumed once; results retain the numeric analysis rows but not every input geometry. Space.from_xyz instead loads every coordinate frame into memory.

Glycan.from_file uses the last XYZ/CP2K frame. Space.from_xyz loads all frames. Automatic trajectory detection uses the first frame. Choose the entry point deliberately when a file contains more than one geometry.

docs.title: Counts and free energy on the sphere
docs.text:
Plot.cremer_pople_sphere pools one count per valid row into (phi, theta) angular bins. The displayed map has longitude 180° − phi and latitude 90° − theta. Histograms are stored in (latitude, longitude) order; stored edges are radians. Five-membered rings cannot use this projection.

Pure chairs contribute to a pole using arbitrary phase 180°; planar and other undefined-angle frames are omitted. Each valid frame receives equal weight, regardless of time spacing, frame order, or dataset length. Longer datasets therefore contribute more counts when pooled.

The default map computes ΔG = −R T ln(N/Nmax) using R=8.314 J/(mol K). Empty bins are masked, and the most populated bin is zero. This is free energy per angular cell, without spherical-area correction or reweighting. Interpolated drawing grids affect only rendering; conformer_counts and free_energy keep the original bin resolution.

A reference library or biased/unequally sampled collection does not automatically represent equilibrium populations. Use quantity="counts" for a descriptive view of such data. See Trajectories for plotting and export examples.

docs.title: RMSD and clustering
docs.text:
Aligned RMSD uses translation removal and a proper Kabsch rotation. It does not allow reflections or symmetry-based atom permutations. The fit and distance use the same atom selection. Single-pair rmsd defaults to all atoms; pairwise matrices and clustering default to heavy atoms.

Clustering uses SciPy hierarchical linkage on condensed RMSD distances. All cluster indices refer back to original inputs; energy-excluded labels are -1. With complete finite energies, representatives minimize the chosen energy attribute. Otherwise they minimize summed within-cluster RMSD (medoids). energy=None explicitly selects medoids.

The complete distance matrix is quadratic in the number of inputs and is calculated before energy filtering. Duplicate removal uses complete linkage, ensuring every pair in a duplicate group is within the threshold. Neither clustering nor duplicate removal changes coordinates or reorders the source Space.

docs.title: Reference-data provenance
docs.text:
The four bundled carbohydrate fixtures come from the CarPpy benchmark set at commit 4589b228cf8772b0f2bd6ccae8bb2f41ad1e7d70. The coordinates and atom order are retained; XYZ comment lines record source paths. glucose_puckers.xyz concatenates 38 reference conformations in source-path order and is not a molecular dynamics trajectory.

The repository's tests/data/README.md documents upstream paths and algorithm provenance. The adaptation adds matmalib object integration, fixed trajectory assignments, ambiguity checks, supported five-membered phase classification, medoid selection, and complete-linkage duplicate removal. CarPpy is not required at runtime. Source tests verify reference atom assignments, all 38 canonical labels, stereochemistry, torsions, cluster behavior, and SNFG drawing geometry.

docs.title: Core API behavior and implementation notes
docs.text: This page complements the generated API reference with behavior that is easy to miss in signatures. Every public class and method in core.py, util.py, calc.py, and elements.py is included below. The walkthroughs are molecules and geometry, I/O, and ensembles.

docs.title: Units, indexing, and mutable data
docs.text:
• Coordinates have no attached unit. The examples and default bond cutoffs assume angstroms; distance and RMSD results retain the input units.
  • Legacy internal-coordinate angles use degrees. Space.diff assumes hartree input and always returns kcal/mol using 627.5095.
  • Use zero-based positions, with Atom.id == position, in legacy connectivity and distance/angle editing code. Dihedral measurements/edits and newer glycan and conformer APIs use atom-list positions independently of Atom.id.
  • State and Data accept arbitrary keyword attributes. They do not validate or infer all required metadata.
  • Atoms, fragment memberships, and state collections are generally shared by reference. Use copy.deepcopy when an independent geometry is required.

docs.title: Atom and Fragment
docs.text: Public member Behavior Atom(coord=None, type=None, valence=None, index=None) Converts coord to a NumPy array; stores type and id=index; initializes mass=None and atoms=None. valence is accepted but unused. Provide a three-component coordinate: the None default is not usable because initialization indexes the resulting scalar array. Atom.coord, .type, .id, .mass Public mutable attributes. Mass is not looked up automatically. Atom.x, .y, .z Initial coordinate snapshots, not synchronized properties. Fragment() Starts with an empty atoms list; additional metadata may be attached by split/glycan routines. Fragment.xyz New array assembled from member atom coordinates. Fragment.Mass New array assembled from member masses; may contain None until supplied.

docs.title: State
docs.text: Public member Behavior / prerequisites State(**kwargs) Stores exactly the supplied attributes. A geometry normally needs atoms, NAtoms, and id. from_file(path, software) Builds through StateBuilder, then sets ID from the containing folder or filename. Gaussian is the documented complete legacy route; use Space.from_xyz for XYZ. xyz, Mass, mass Coordinate array, mass array, and sum of masses. Arrays are newly assembled. mass requires usable mass values. element_symbol(A) Returns a symbol for atomic number 1–118, accepting an integer or matching numeric string; unknown keys raise KeyError. add_atoms(atom), remove_atoms(atom) Append/remove a single Atom object; do not update NAtoms, IDs, bonds, or fragments. Return None. measure_internal(atom_list) Dispatches to StateEditor.measure. Distances return floats, angles return (degrees, axis), dihedrals return degrees. set_internal(atom_list, val) Dispatches a mutation to the corresponding editor method for 2/3/4 selections. Unsupported lengths do nothing. Return is None. connectivity_matrix(distXX=1.65, distXH=1.15) Infers a symmetric distance-threshold matrix and sets graph and Nmols. Requires consistent NAtoms, atom IDs and positions. Returns None; no bond orders/PBC. Hydrogen ambiguity branch is currently broken. system_split() Reads graph, stores connected components as mols (Fragments sharing atoms). Returns None. show(width=600, height=600) Displays a Py3Dmol stick view in a compatible notebook environment; requires id and NAtoms, rounds displayed coordinates to three decimals, returns None.

docs.title: StateEditor
docs.text:
StateEditor(state) retains the supplied state; edits mutate it. Static measurement methods accept all Atom objects, or all Python integer positions with state=...; get_dihedral additionally accepts NumPy integer positions. Avoid collinear triples, coincident atoms, and mixed selections.

Public method Return / mutation get_distance(atom_list, state=None) Euclidean distance, expected length 2. get_angle(atom_list, state=None) (degrees, cross_product_axis), expected length 3; axis is unnormalized. get_dihedral(atom_list, state=None, ax=False) Signed degrees in [-180, 180], using the shared, translation-invariant atan2 convention. Requires exactly four finite three-component coordinates; negative/out-of-range positions, coincident central atoms, and collinear triples raise ValueError. With ax=True, returns (degrees, cross_product_axis); the compatibility axis is unnormalized and can be zero for planar geometry. measure(atom_list, state=None) Dispatches by selection length 2/3/4; other lengths return None. adjacent_atoms(conn_mat, at) NumPy array of nonzero neighbor positions in row at. connect_atoms(state, at1, at2) Sets both matrix entries to one; does not update the graph. disconnect_atoms(state, at1, at2) Sets both matrix entries to zero; does not update the graph. determine_carried_atoms(state, atom_list) Temporarily removes a bond and returns the Atom objects in the second atom's connected component, normally restoring the bond. If the matrix stays connected, returns None after printing and currently leaves that bond removed. set_distance(atom_list, new_distance) Requires two Python integer positions; translates the carried component. New distance uses input units. Returns None. set_angle(atom_list, new_ang) Requires three Python integer positions; rotates the third atom's component around the middle atom, in degrees. Returns None. set_dihedral(atom_list, new_dih, incr=False, axis_pos="bond", threshold=0.1) Requires four distinct Python or NumPy integer positions within the state. Rotation requires a finite symmetric conn_mat indexed by atom position and containing the selected bond. With incr=True, adds the requested angle. "bond" rotates the third atom's component about the central bond, preserving connectivity and rejecting cyclic bonds. "term" uses a parallel axis through the last atom and rotates atoms beyond it, leaving the selected quartet unchanged. Targets/increments wrap modulo 360°; finite targets and a finite, nonnegative tolerance are required. Returns None.

The setters only manipulate geometry; there is no relaxation, collision checking, ring-closure constraint, or automatic topology update. set_dihedral uses the central-bond direction for a stable rotation axis, supports exact 0° and ±180° targets, and rejects unsupported axis_pos values. Its threshold only skips changes at or below the angular tolerance; it does not alter the target to avoid planar geometry. The distance/angle setters and direct determine_carried_atoms calls retain the legacy connectivity limitations listed above. Keep a copy and remeasure outputs.

Dihedral compatibility: the sign of get_dihedral and its measure/measure_internal wrappers has been corrected to match the existing glycan torsion convention. The legacy translation-dependent sign error and small offsets at 0°/±180° are also fixed. Saved legacy results should be recomputed from coordinates, and absolute/incremental targets for set_dihedral now follow the corrected sign. Glycan torsions and ring calculations retain their existing convention. See the formula and worked example.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: Public member Behavior Data(**kwargs) Attribute container, typically with a NumPy data array. repr(data) Returns Data({...}) with stored attributes. Data.from_file(path, software, **kwargs) Uses DataBuilder; accepts "cp2k", "gromacs", or "csv". Metadata and supported options are forwarded to the builder.

docs.title: Space
docs.text:
Public member Behavior Space(states=None, theory=None, input_path=None, output_path=None) Holds a list of states and calculation settings. Stores a provided list by reference; creates a fresh list if omitted. from_xyz(path, *, glycans=False) Reads all XYZ frames into States or Glycans, assigns frame IDs and paths, rejects empty trajectories. from_dir(path, software="gaussian") Reads <path>/<immediate_subdirectory>/input.log for each subdirectory. Only Gaussian is implemented. Order follows directory enumeration. energies, free_energies, enthalpies Lists of E, F, H respectively, skipping states missing that attribute. diff(states=None, quant="E") Relative-to-minimum kcal/mol values from hartree E/F/H; accepts a list of indices or State objects. Invalid quantity raises ValueError, missing attributes raise AttributeError. Empty selection falls back to all states. sum(states, quant="E") Sum of original-unit E/F/H across State objects. Any integer states argument means all states. Invalid/missing quantities print an error and return None. add(state) Appends one State or every State in a list; no copy or uniqueness check. remove(state) Intended for object/index removal, but currently fails immediately with UnboundLocalError; use list methods on .states. sort(val="E") In-place attribute sort; prints errors and returns None. table(sort="E") In-place sort and printed tabulate table; fixed headings require consistent energy metadata. Returns None; requires separately installed tabulate. rmsd_matrix(**kwargs) Delegates to conformers.rmsd_matrix; default aligned heavy-atom RMSDs. cluster(threshold=1.0, **kwargs) Delegates to cluster_conformers; returns ClusterResult. remove_duplicates(threshold=0.1, **kwargs) Complete-linkage representatives as a new Space; original collection retained, selected states shared. The linkage method is fixed internally. to_file(software="gaussian") Passes stored theory/output path and self to InputBuilder; Gaussian works with required settings. XYZ requires the lower-level iterable path described below. Returns None.

Space is not itself iterable or subscriptable: use space.states. See ensemble walkthroughs and conformer analysis.

docs.title: StateBuilder
docs.text:
StateBuilder(path, software) stores its inputs. Parser methods mutate the builder; build() constructs a new State from all builder attributes, computes legacy connectivity, and splits components.

Public method Behavior element_symbol(A) Same 1–118 atomic-number mapping as State.element_symbol. gaussian() Parses selected Gaussian route types, geometry, available energy/thermal fields, vibrational data, and lower-triangular NMR couplings. Mutates builder attributes and returns None. Format-sensitive; not every Gaussian output layout is supported. cp2k_geom() Reads the last NAtoms coordinate lines from an XYZ trajectory. Atom IDs are currently unset because indices are passed positionally as valence. Prefer Space.from_xyz. orca() Incomplete optimization/energy-only parser. An energy match may return the builder, but it does not supply the geometry required by build; the optimization branch has path and variable errors. build() Dispatches "cp2k", "gaussian", "orca"; unknown software raises ValueError. Returns a State only if parsing, connectivity, and splitting succeed.

docs.title: DataBuilder
docs.text:
DataBuilder(path, software, **kwargs) retains every keyword as an attribute. Methods populate .data and metadata on the builder; build() returns a Data with a shallow copy of those attributes.

Public method Behavior csv(skiprows=0, dtype=float, delimiter=",") Calls np.loadtxt; attributes supplied to the builder override these method defaults/arguments. Returns None. cp2k_md(colvar=None, timestep=None) For XYZ, computes a legacy coordinate or dispatches structured Cremer–Pople analysis. Explicit non-None method arguments override builder colvar/timestep. For .metadynLog, reads the numeric table unchanged. Sets time_unit="fs". Returns None. gromacs() Parses a limited XVG numeric table/header or a square uppercase-key XPM matrix. Values are not converted. Returns None. build() Dispatches "cp2k", "gromacs", "csv"; unknown software raises ValueError. Returns Data.

CP2K coordinate extraction requires colvar and timestep, except .metadynLog table loading. Two/four atom selections produce distance/dihedral data; three-atom tuples currently fail numeric array assembly. XYZ selections follow file order, not arbitrary colvar order. The observable="cremer_pople" route requires timestep, accepts rings, degrees, conn_mat, distXX, distXH, and classify, and uses the validated trajectory implementation. Other CP2K/GROMACS suffixes may yield a container with no data attribute because those parser branches do not reject unknown file formats.

docs.title: InputBuilder
docs.text:
InputBuilder(path=None, theory=None, software="gaussian", space=None) only stores settings. build(space, theory, software, path, names=None) sets all these again plus names, then invokes a writer. For predictable behavior call build; gaussian() reads self.names, which the constructor does not initialize.

Public method Behavior element_number(A) Case-sensitive element symbol to integer atomic number, 1–118; unknown symbols raise KeyError. gaussian() Expects space.states. Creates <path>/<id>/input.com, rounds coordinates to three decimals, mutates the dispersion setting, and overwrites existing files. Non-None names currently raises an error; set state IDs directly. xyz() Expects an iterable of states, such as space.states. Creates <path>/<id>/geometry.xyz with three-decimal coordinates; no trajectory concatenation. fhiaims() Legacy incomplete writer with a site-specific basis directory, absolute geometry output path, and Atom/string formatting error. Do not rely on it to produce valid FHI-aims inputs. build(space, theory, software, path, names=None) Dispatches "gaussian", "xyz", "fhiaims"; unknown values silently do nothing. Returns None.

The output parent directory must already exist. Use unique directory-safe state.id values and review generated input before submitting it to external software. Required Gaussian theory keys are disp, nprocs, mem, method, basis_set, jobtype, charge, and multiplicity; optional keys are other_options and extra. See the complete input generation example.

docs.title: Element mappings
docs.text:
matmalib.elements contains the standard symbols for elements 1 through 118. ELEMENT_SYMBOLS has string atomic-number keys; ELEMENT_NUMBERS has case-sensitive symbol keys and integer values. These are ordinary dictionaries, not a periodic-table database: masses, isotopes, radii, and valences are not supplied.

from matmalib import State, StateBuilder
from matmalib.calc import InputBuilder
from matmalib.elements import ELEMENT_SYMBOLS, ELEMENT_NUMBERS

print("Elements:", len(ELEMENT_SYMBOLS))
for number in (1, 6, 8, 26, 79, 118):
    symbol = ELEMENT_SYMBOLS[str(number)]
    print(number, symbol, ELEMENT_NUMBERS[symbol])

print(State.element_symbol(26))
print(StateBuilder.element_symbol("79"))
print(InputBuilder.element_number("Og"))

The wrappers convert numeric inputs to strings before lookup, so State.element_symbol(6) and State.element_symbol("6") both return "C". 6.0, zero, missing elements, and wrong symbol case are not normalized and raise KeyError. Try changing: look up another integer from 1 through 118, then compare direct dictionary lookup with the wrappers.

docs.title: Sample data and attribution
docs.text:
The live examples use the repository's small, public test fixtures. Each build copies them directly from tests/data; the runner sees the same content at data/....

Download Purpose glucose.xyz A glucose geometry for recognition, numbering, and measurement glycan.xyz A multi-residue carbohydrate for linkage analysis glucose_puckers.xyz The 38-reference glucose conformer ensemble fucosylated_trisaccharide.xyz A branched three-residue glycan for SNFG and torsions

These are demonstration and regression fixtures, not an equilibrium molecular-dynamics trajectory. Population maps of their conformers illustrate an algorithm; they do not establish physical free energies. Tutorials explicitly label synthetic trajectories and numerical data.

docs.title: Scientific provenance
docs.text:
Carbohydrate detection, atom numbering, and six-membered canonical pucker classification adapt work from CarPpy. The detailed fixture provenance, upstream commit, adaptation scope, and benchmark construction are recorded in the data README.

Cremer–Pople coordinates follow Cremer and Pople, JACS (1975). Glycan symbol conventions follow the Symbol Nomenclature for Glycans (SNFG). The library's exact phase, ordering, angle, and classification conventions are described in Units and conventions.

The website uses Material for MkDocs, mkdocstrings, and Pyodide. Browser calculations use NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, NetworkX, colormaps, and py3Dmol.

docs.title: MLMD configuration reference
docs.text:
Import the interface with from matmalib import mlmd. Configuration classes are nested dataclasses: mlmd.MDConfig(...), for example. The tables below are generated from the checkout at build time, so their defaults match the browser bundle and API reference. Each table lists fields declared or overridden by that class; inherited fields are linked explicitly.

Constructing a config or mlmd() does not load models, run a simulation, or fully validate the configuration. Geometry-dependent and operation-specific checks happen when the operation starts. Use dataclasses.replace(config, steps=...) to derive another configuration without mutating the original.

docs.title: Choose an operation
docs.text:
Call Configuration Result simulation.minimize(system, config) MinimizationConfig Relaxed State, or output Path simulation.equilibrate(system, config) EquilibrationConfig Final State with masses/momenta, or output Path simulation.run_md(system, config) MDConfig Streamed trajectory Path simulation.restart_md(checkpoint, steps=...) Saved configuration; additional-step count supplied to the method New trajectory segment Path simulation.solvate(solute, solvent, config) SolvationConfig Packed State/output Path, or Data for a dry run simulation.analyze_metadynamics(config) AnalysisConfig Analysis Data, or output directory with output_format="files"

Simulation inputs accept a supported XYZ/PDB path, a matmalib State, or ASE Atoms. The geometry is copied. minimize, equilibrate, and solvate accept output=... and output_format="state"/"xyz"; requesting XYZ requires an output path. simulation.data holds diagnostics for the most recent operation, so save a reference before starting another operation. Trajectories stream to files rather than accumulating frames in memory.

Worked examples: running simulations, checkpoints, solvation, metadynamics, and FES analysis. See the API reference for exact method signatures.

docs.title: Calculator selection
docs.text:
mlmd(...) argument Default Meaning model_path None Default four-member AIMNet2-2025 B97-3c/D3 ensemble; a supported alias, inference-file path, or sequence selects other AIMNet weights device None Device selection passed to AIMNet; specify "cpu" or a supported CUDA device for the local environment compile_model False Pass model-compilation preference to AIMNet calculator None Supply an ASE calculator instead of constructing AIMNet adapters model_kwargs None Additional AIMNet calculator options (stored as an empty dictionary when omitted); supply device and compile_model through the explicit arguments

calculator and model_path are mutually exclusive. Injected calculators are used directly; model construction settings do not configure them. The default model lookup and downloads occur at the first operation needing a calculator. AIMNet adapters are cached separately by charge, multiplicity, and periodicity. Use the same potential, weights, and numerical environment when continuing a checkpoint. A restart does not serialize the model itself.

docs.title: Units and indexing
docs.text:
Quantity MLMD convention Coordinates/cell/distances Å Energy and force eV and eV/Å Integration and damping times fs Temperature and pressure K and bar Atomic masses Atomic mass units Density g/mL, total system mass divided by cell volume fixed_atoms Zero-based positions in the input system Generated PLUMED atoms One-based atom indices Generated PLUMED distance, energy, time nm, kJ/mol, ps Generated PLUMED angle/torsion widths Radians Analysis free energies kJ/mol internally; Plot.fes_1d can convert its displayed energy axis

Custom PLUMED input can declare different units. Keep its widths, walls, grids, and analysis metadata consistent. A units label does not rescale the input CV values.

docs.title: SystemConfig
docs.text:
Inherited by minimization, production MD, and equilibration.

Field Type Default cell Any None pbc bool \| tuple[bool, bool, bool] \| None None charge float \| None None multiplicity int \| None None min_distance float 0.5 fixed_atoms tuple[int, ...] () fix_com bool False shake_hydrogens bool False shake_cutoff float 1.3 shake_tolerance float 1e-06
  • cell and pbc override input metadata when supplied; otherwise existing settings are retained. Periodic geometry needs a valid cell.
  • charge and multiplicity supply electronic-state metadata. They do not change atom count or automatically add counterions.
  • min_distance rejects initial atom pairs closer than the threshold, including periodic neighbors; zero disables this check.
  • fixed_atoms freezes selected atom positions. fix_com creates a persistent center-of-mass constraint.
  • shake_hydrogens constrains the lengths of nearby atom pairs involving hydrogen within shake_cutoff, at shake_tolerance, and also fixes the center of mass. Pair selection uses distance, not chemical bond order. NPT and Nose–Hoover-chain dynamics reject constrained systems.

docs.title: MinimizationConfig
docs.text:
Inherits every SystemConfig field.

Field Type Default optimizer str 'FIRE' fmax float 0.05 steps int 10000 maxstep float 0.1 optimizer_kwargs dict[str, Any] {} require_convergence bool True trajectory str \| PathLike \| None None trajectory_interval int 1 log_file str \| PathLike \| None None overwrite bool False

optimizer selects an optimizer class exported by ase.optimize, matched case-insensitively, such as FIRE, BFGS, LBFGS, or BFGSLineSearch. optimizer_kwargs forwards additional optimizer settings; use the dedicated fields instead for maxstep, trajectory, and log output. fmax is the force convergence threshold, steps the iteration limit, and maxstep limits optimizer displacement when the selected optimizer explicitly accepts that argument. FIRE enables downhill_check by default. require_convergence=True raises when the threshold is not reached. Inspect the convergence report when deliberately disabling that requirement.

trajectory and log_file enable optional minimization output. trajectory_interval controls saved optimizer frames. overwrite=False protects existing outputs; even with overwriting enabled, conflicting input/output paths are rejected. See minimization and production.

docs.title: MDConfig
docs.text:
Inherits every SystemConfig field.

Field Type Default steps int 10000 timestep_fs float 0.5 temperature_K float 300.0 ensemble str 'NVT' thermostat str 'langevin' barostat str 'mtk' thermostat_time_fs float 100.0 barostat_time_fs float 1000.0 pressure_bar float 1.0 compressibility_per_bar float 4.57e-05 thermostat_chain int 3 barostat_chain int 3 seed int \| None None initialize_velocities bool \| None None remove_com_motion bool True hydrogen_mass float \| None None heavy_mass_multiplier float 1.0 max_velocity_angstrom_fs float \| None None max_force_eV_A float \| None 150.0 trajectory str \| PathLike 'trajectory.xyz' trajectory_interval int 10 wrap_output bool False log_file str \| PathLike \| None 'md.log' log_interval int 10 checkpoint_interval int 1000 checkpoint_file str \| PathLike \| None 'auto' mode str 'md' metadynamics mlmd.MetadynamicsConfig \| None None minimization mlmd.MinimizationConfig \| None None equilibration mlmd.EquilibrationConfig \| None None continue_equilibration_bias bool False overwrite bool False

Integration and ensembles. steps × timestep_fs is the duration requested for this phase. NVE uses velocity Verlet; temperature_K initializes velocities when requested rather than applying a thermostat. NVT supports "langevin", "berendsen", and "nose-hoover"; Nose–Hoover chains reject constraints. NPT supports isotropic "mtk" or "berendsen" dynamics, requires full three-dimensional PBC and stress from the calculator, and disallows constraints. Ensemble, thermostat, and barostat names are matched case-insensitively. thermostat_time_fs and barostat_time_fs set coupling times; the chain fields configure the chain integrators. NPT includes its thermostat; the NVT thermostat selector does not choose it. pressure_bar is the NPT target; compressibility_per_bar is required by the Berendsen barostat and should match the material.

Velocities and masses. initialize_velocities=None preserves existing momenta and initializes when absent; True requests fresh thermal velocities, and False requires input momenta/velocities. A plain geometry without them is rejected with False. seed controls initialization and stochastic dynamics. remove_com_motion removes translation only when initializing an unconstrained system with more than one atom; persistent fixing is controlled separately by fix_com. hydrogen_mass replaces hydrogen masses, while heavy_mass_multiplier scales other masses. Existing velocities are preserved when masses change. These settings alter the dynamics and are not mass-conserving repartitioning. max_velocity_angstrom_fs and max_force_eV_A are abort thresholds, not clipping operations.

Files and diagnostics. trajectory, trajectory_interval, wrap_output, log_file, and log_interval control streamed output and its cadence. Wrapping changes the written coordinates. checkpoint_interval controls periodic checkpoint saves; a final checkpoint is also written. checkpoint_file="auto" derives a name from the run output, while None disables checkpointing. Reusing output paths requires overwrite=True. Checkpoints and trajectory files are distinct; see restart behavior.

Phases and bias. Set mode="metadynamics" together with metadynamics=MetadynamicsConfig(...) for a biased run. Optional minimization and equilibration configs prepare the input before production. continue_equilibration_bias=True keeps one live PLUMED instance across compatible equilibration and production phases; it requires matching bias settings and timestep. It is not a replacement for a disk checkpoint.

docs.title: EquilibrationConfig
docs.text:
Inherits MDConfig, including its SystemConfig fields. These defaults are overridden:

Field Type Default steps int 2000 thermostat_time_fs float 10.0 max_force_eV_A float \| None None trajectory str \| PathLike \| None None log_file str \| PathLike \| None 'equilibration.log'

Equilibration uses a shorter thermostat time and disables the production force-abort threshold by default. Its trajectory is optional. Masses, cell, and momenta can pass into production when a returned State is reused. Equilibration can also save ordinary or biased checkpoints. It supports an optional minimization but rejects a nested equilibration configuration.

docs.title: SolvationConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default cell float \| tuple[float, float, float] 30.0 density_g_ml float 1.0 counterion Any None counterion_gap float 0.5 packmol str \| PathLike 'packmol' tolerance float 2.0 nloop int 1000 timeout float 600.0 seed int 12345 volume_samples int 200000 vdw_radii dict[str, float] {} work_dir str \| PathLike \| None None dry_run bool False charge float \| None None multiplicity int 1 overwrite bool False

cell defines a cubic or orthorhombic periodic box. density_g_ml targets total density, including the solute and optional single counterion; solvent count is an integer, so inspect the achieved density. counterion_gap separates the solute/ion van der Waals surfaces; their positions are fixed during packing only. volume_samples and element-keyed vdw_radii configure diagnostic molecular sphere-union volume estimates, which are not subtracted from the cell volume for density counting. The radii also affect fixed-molecule placement.

packmol selects the executable; tolerance, nloop, timeout, and seed control packing. A supplied work_dir preserves generated packing inputs and reports. dry_run=True requires this directory, skips Packmol execution, and returns Data; omit geometry output arguments for a dry run. charge=None sums component charge metadata; multiplicities are not summed, so set the complete system's multiplicity explicitly. overwrite governs replacement of generated files. See the solvation walkthrough for diagnostics and periodic collision checks.

docs.title: MetadynamicsConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default plumed_file str \| PathLike \| None None input_lines tuple[str, ...] \| None None save_input str \| PathLike \| None None cv str 'DISTANCE' cv_label str 'cv' atoms tuple[int, ...] (1, 2) metad_label str 'metad' metad_arg str \| None None sigma float 0.02 height_kj_mol float 2.0 pace int 300 biasfactor float 10.0 temperature_K float \| None None hills_file str \| PathLike 'HILLS' colvar_file str \| PathLike 'COLVAR' colvar_stride int 10 colvar_arg str \| None None wall_type str \| None None wall_label str 'wall' wall_arg str \| None None wall_at float 0.35 wall_kappa float 150000.0 wall_exp int 2 wall_eps float 1.0 wall_offset float 0.0 calc_rct bool \| None None grid_auto bool \| None None grid_min float 0.0 grid_max float \| None None grid_bins int \| None None grid_spacing float 0.002 log_file str \| PathLike \| None None

Input. Supply either plumed_file or input_lines for custom actions, or use the generated-input settings. Custom input controls its own CVs, units, bias parameters, output paths, and restart directives; generated fields do not override its actions. save_input writes the resolved input for reproducibility. log_file selects the native PLUMED log.

Collective variable and deposition. Generated input supports DISTANCE, ANGLE, and TORSION. cv_label names the CV and atoms selects its unique one-based indices. metad_label names the bias; metad_arg=None uses cv_label. sigma, height_kj_mol, pace, and biasfactor configure well-tempered Gaussian deposition; the bias factor must exceed one. temperature_K=None uses the dynamics temperature; an explicit positive value overrides the generated METAD temperature without changing the MD thermostat temperature. Keep these temperatures physically consistent for your intended protocol.

History/output. For generated input, hills_file records deposited Gaussians. colvar_file and colvar_stride control observable output. With colvar_arg=None, the implementation selects available CV/bias/normalization columns; an explicit value selects requested PLUMED fields, omitting references to disabled wall and normalization fields. Generated HILLS/COLVAR paths must be distinct and contain no whitespace.

Walls. wall_type selects an upper or lower wall. wall_label and wall_arg name the wall and its argument; wall_arg=None uses the CV. wall_at, wall_kappa, wall_exp, wall_eps, and wall_offset configure its position and shape in the PLUMED unit system.

Normalization grid. grid_auto, grid_min, grid_max, grid_bins, and grid_spacing control the metadynamics grid. calc_rct controls normalization needed for reweighted analysis. With automatic defaults, normalization and a grid are enabled for a fixed-cell, fully periodic scalar distance CV; a complete explicit grid also enables normalization unless calc_rct=False. An explicit grid requires both grid_max and grid_bins, with grid_min < grid_max. NPT and other CVs need suitable explicit bounds when requesting normalization. Use the metadynamics tutorial before enabling a bias: generated defaults are not an experiment-specific CV definition.

docs.title: AnalysisConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default colvar Any None hills str \| PathLike \| None None fes_file str \| PathLike \| None None plumed_input str \| PathLike \| None None plumed str \| PathLike \| None None cv str \| None None temperature float \| None None energy_unit str \| None None time_unit str \| None None cv_unit str \| None None bins int 100 grid_range tuple[float, float] \| None None energy_column str 'file.free' rbias_column str \| None None bias_column str \| None None rct_column str \| None None additional_bias tuple[str, ...] \| None None start_time float \| None None end_time float \| None None upper_wall tuple[float, float] \| None None keep_wall bool False reactant tuple[float, float] \| None None product tuple[float, float] \| None None kappa float 1.0 infrequent bool False acceleration_column str \| None None smooth_window int 11 plot bool False output_dir str \| PathLike \| None None overwrite bool False

Inputs and metadata. fes_file loads an existing one-dimensional free-energy grid; hills requests PLUMED reconstruction; colvar supplies samples or independent infrequent runs. Do not provide both hills and fes_file. plumed_input supplies action/units metadata and can resolve associated files. plumed selects the native command for reconstruction. Explicit cv, temperature, energy_unit, time_unit, and cv_unit settings override inferred values. Supported energy units are kJ/mol, kcal/mol, and eV; time units are fs, ps, ns, and s. Output energy arrays use kJ/mol. cv_unit labels the coordinate without rescaling it.

Profiles and weights. bins and grid_range define a histogram/reconstruction grid; grid_range cannot resample an existing fes_file. energy_column names the existing-grid free-energy column. rbias_column supplies normalized bias directly, or bias_column and rct_column supply its components. additional_bias names recorded static-bias columns to remove through population reweighting. start_time and end_time restrict the COLVAR population histogram to an inclusive time window; they do not truncate first-passage runs or HILLS. upper_wall=(at, kappa) subtracts a quadratic upper wall from a supplied or reconstructed FES. keep_wall disables automatic wall removal and conflicts with upper_wall; for COLVAR, explicitly named additional_bias columns are still removed.

Basins and kinetics. reactant and product specify non-overlapping CV intervals; provide both or neither. Absent explicit intervals, a profile may receive inferred basin assignments. kappa (greater than zero and at most one) enters Eyring proxies and the rate-to-activation-energy conversion; it does not change the first-passage event/exposure rate estimator. infrequent=True requests first-passage analysis of independent COLVAR runs; explicit basin ranges are required. acceleration_column selects a cumulative acceleration factor instead of integrating raw bias_column. Multiple COLVAR inputs are accepted only for this independent-run mode. Rate interpretation requires the assumptions discussed in FES and kinetics analysis.

Display and export. smooth_window is zero (off) or an odd integer of at least five, configuring local cubic least-squares smoothing. Raw thermodynamics retain the unsmoothed profile and unsampled gaps. output_dir enables CSV/JSON output; plot=True additionally requests a PNG and requires that directory. overwrite protects existing exports. For directory return instead of Data, call analyze_metadynamics(config, output_format="files").

The current analysis supports one CV and rejects FES grids marked periodic. COLVAR histograms treat the coordinate as a line and do not join its periodic endpoints, so boundary-crossing basins are unsupported. It has no automatic convergence certificate or uncertainty estimator. Compare independent sampling, inspect diagnostics, and follow the analysis tutorial.

docs.title: Library additions and deliberate differences
docs.text:
The library adds NVE, additional NVT thermostats, isotropic NPT integrators, State inputs/outputs, explicit output protection, and atomic restart checkpoints every 1,000 steps and at completion. By default, MD runs save positions, velocities, RNG state, thermostat/barostat state and constraints, including ordinary MD and any custom PLUMED input. Generated metadynamics also saves its bias history.

Library defaults do not encode the original experiment's atom numbers, box, density, two-million-step duration, or fine-tuned fifth ensemble member. Set the configs explicitly to reproduce that experiment. The old velocity-cap code was commented out; the library offers an optional velocity abort guard instead. Older nested script copies' retry-and-continue minimization behavior is replaced by an explicit convergence result and failure by default.

For fixed-cell periodic distance CVs, normalized metadynamics weights and an automatic grid are enabled by default. For other CVs and NPT, supply suitable explicit grid bounds to enable normalization, or reconstruct the FES from HILLS. Ordinary MD and generated PLUMED input support automatic restart. Custom PLUMED input still produces checkpoints, but restoring its bias requires action-specific restart files. The 1D analysis retains the source script's limitations on multidimensional and periodic-boundary-crossing free-energy profiles.

Script-only process management (package installation, Python re-execution, hardcoded cluster library paths, global compilation environment changes and CLI/IDE globals) is replaced by optional package dependencies and explicit API arguments. Select a timestamped output_dir in Python when needed. Training, dataset conversion, model export, and training TUI utilities are outside this simulation interface.

Start with running MLMD simulations, then follow the solvation, metadynamics, restart, and FES analysis tutorials. The configuration reference lists every setting and its current default.
